analyst_view.overall: Early view: Bournemouth are the form team, with four straight league wins and a winning run in all competitions that continued 2-1 at Ipswich, while Forest sit 16th but arrive lifted by a 3-1 win over Manchester City under Glasner, with Liam Delap scoring twice. Bournemouth are without Alex Toth for months and Alex Scott's thigh problem is still being managed.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean slightly higher: Evanilson is scoring for a Bournemouth side that has won its last four league games, and Forest just put three past City with Delap leading the line. Both attacks arrive in better shape than their defences.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners and I see no strong reason to move. Bournemouth's wide men, Tavernier and Kluivert among them, should win their share at home, and nothing in either team's news shifts the balance.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. Bournemouth were booked three times in their win at Ipswich, which fits the site's figure, and Forest's position near the bottom keeps their intensity high. Without a named referee I keep the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 26 shots. I lean slightly higher: Marco Rose's Bournemouth play at a high tempo and are full of confidence at home, and Forest showed against City that they will commit players forward. Both sides have been scoring freely in their latest games.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, which looks about right. Bournemouth's forwards are finishing well, but Forest held City to a single goal at the City Ground, so I do not move from the site.
